FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION

Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Multiple myeloma
Clinical Details: Bone marrow aspirate with 8% plasma cells
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referring Institution: [redacted location]

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH Analysis for Multiple Myeloma Panel

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on CD138+ enriched plasma cells from bone marrow aspirate using the following probe sets:
1. IGH break apart probe (Vysis LSI IGH Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe)
2. 1q21/SRD(1p36) dual color probe set
3. Multi-color probe set for D5S23,D5S721/CEP9/CEP15
4. CLL panel including TP53/ATM and D13S319/13q34/CEP12

A minimum of 100 interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set when possible. Plasma cell enrichment was performed using CD138 immunomagnetic selection.

RESULTS

IGH/CCND1 Rearrangement [t(11;14)]:
Result: POSITIVE
Abnormal cells: 6/100 (6%)
Pattern: Split signal pattern consistent with IGH/CCND1 rearrangement

TP53 (17p13.1):
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

SRD (1p36):
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

D13S319 (13q14):
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

1q21 Region:
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

ATM (11q22.3):
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

Chromosomes 5, 9, and 15:
Result: UNINFORMATIVE - Low plasma cell count

TECHNICAL NOTES
Due to the low plasma cell percentage (8%) in the bone marrow aspirate, analysis was limited. Only the IGH/CCND1 rearrangement analysis yielded interpretable results. Additional probes were uninformative due to insufficient plasma cell count for reliable analysis.

INTERPRETATION
Interphase FISH analysis detected an IGH/CCND1 rearrangement [t(11;14)] in 6% of cells analyzed. This is an established cytogenetic abnormality in multiple myeloma, typically associated with lymphoplasmacytic morphology and CD20 expression. The t(11;14) translocation results in overexpression of cyclin D1 and is found in approximately 15-20% of multiple myeloma cases.

Analysis for additional prognostic markers including TP53 deletion, 1p36 deletion, 13q14 deletion, 1q21 gain, ATM deletion, and hyperdiploidy was uninformative due to the low plasma cell count in the specimen.
